chunks: That was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Ali ibn Asbat from Musa ibn Sa'dan from some of his men who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man came to him and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you think about two young men who were close companions (consanguineous milk-brothers or close friends), and a boy was born to this one and a girl to the other? Is it permissible for the son of this one to marry the daughter of that one?' He said, 'Yes, glory be to Allah, why would it not be permissible for him?'
He said to him, 'He was a close friend of his.' He said, 'And glory be to Allah, even if he was, there is no harm.'
He said, 'There used to be between them what there is between young men (intimacy).' He said, 'There is no harm.'

He said, 'He used to do it to him.' He said, so he turned his face away, then answered him while he was covering himself with his arm, and said, 'If what was from him was less than full intimacy (al-iqab), there is no harm in him marrying, but if he had fully intimate (al-iqab), it is not permissible for him to marry.'

key_terms.الْإِيقَابِ: Full intimacy or sexual intercourse (specifically in the context of male-male relations in this hadith)
key_terms.مُصْطَحِبَيْنِ: Two people who lay together, often implying close companionship or milk-kinship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage between the children of two men who were close intimate friends in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *al-Iqab* (mutual sexual intimacy) as a cause of marriage prohibition (*mahramiyah*) between the children of the intimate partners, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the nuance of this ruling by distinguishing between partial intimacy, which does not prohibit marriage, and full intercourse, which does, highlighting the importance of specific factual determination in legal judgments. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise definitions of physical acts in deriving familial prohibitions beyond mere lineage.
